_comment._span_caveat: THE SPAN ABOVE IS SIZED FROM Ky 3.646, WHICH THIS RUN EXISTS TO REPLACE. 3.646 came from fsm_bodey_par2.dat, taken before the 2026-08-06 retune; K is in NORMALIZED units, so it scales with (dim-1)/2 and does not carry across an ROI-size change (the same optical px/V reads half as large at 64x64 as at 32x32). If par2 was not taken at 64x64, the real travel here is nearer +-7 px than +-14. This degrades safely rather than silently: gain_test excludes any level past resp_max 0.9 and reports the sample count, so a too-small span shows up as a noisy fit and a too-large one as excluded end levels. Check the first run's log and re-size the span before trusting the number.

params._roi_note: ROI and exposure copied from steering_par_fsp.json so this measures the plant the loop actually runs against. ROI re-derived 2026-08-06 to 1084/418 (find_roi put the beam at 1088/406; the residual is the 4-px/2-px ASI ROI grid) -- the earlier 644/318 was an unverified ASI662MM carry-over. The beam walks several px per hour: re-probe with contrib/probe_frame.json and re-derive with contrib/find_roi.py once |park| exceeds ~2 px.

pipeline._comment: frame -> UDP viewer, so the beam can be watched walking the staircase

pipeline._note: fit_com, matching steering_par_fsp.json exactly, so the gain is measured through the same sensor the loop uses -- steering moved from center_of_mass to fit_com on 2026-08-06 and a K measured through the old estimator is a K for a loop that no longer exists. The 55x55 window also swallows the whole +-14 px staircase without the window ever having to walk, which the old 20x20 could not.
pipeline._provenance: Values MEASURED 2026-08-06 by contrib/com_survey_run.sh at this ROI/exposure: beam sigma 6.55 px, amplitude 213.9 over background 1.74. window 55 = +/-4 sigma; sigma_min/max and min_amplitude are 0.3x/4x/0.1x of measured. RE-RUN com_survey_run.sh and re-derive after any refocus or source change.
pipeline._holds: gain_test's frozen-level guard STILL WORKS against fit_com: a rejected fit re-publishes the previous coordinate bit-identically, which is exactly the all-samples-equal signature gain_test excludes on. reacquire_after is 300 here rather than the old 10, matching steering: at 10 the 4.70 Hz source chop (dark stretches median 3 frames, p90 49, max 201) would drop acquisition several times per second and re-search the window mid-staircase.
pipeline._replaced: Replaced this center_of_mass block, kept for reversibility: {"_note":"tracked 20x20, threshold 5, min_peak 40 -- the steering configuration exactly, so the gain is measured through the same sensor the loop uses. reacquire_after 10 matters more here than in a sweep: a staircase moves the beam 1.5 px per level, and a lost window would otherwise hold its last coordinate for the rest of the run (gain_test does detect that and excludes the level, but re-acquiring is better than losing the tail).","region_height":20,"region_width":20,"threshold":5,"min_peak":40,"track":true,"reacquire_after":10}

pipeline._comment: CoM -> UDP viewer so the tracked centroid can be overlaid

pipeline._note1: THE TEST. Drives element 0 (y) and watches element 0 of the CoM ([y, x]); x stays at 0 command, i.e. parked at 0 V.
pipeline._note2: 21 levels at 1 s each = 21 s of staircase, plus 10 s warmup and 2 s of ramp at each end. settle_frac 0.5 throws away the first half of every level and averages the second: at fs 2310 Hz (64x64, exp 400, measured 2026-08-06 -- not the 3788 Hz this note used to assume) that is ~1150 samples per level, against an FSM that settles in well under a millisecond.
pipeline._updown: off, so this is the 21 s run as specified. Turn it on (42 s) for two things a single ramp cannot give: hysteresis, and a drift-corrected gain -- in a plain rising staircase the command and the clock are the same axis, so drift and gain are collinear and the device declines to split them. Worth doing whenever a K matters, since the beam here walks several px per hour.
pipeline._pixel_scale: MUST TRACK THE ROI: (dim-1)/2 = 31.5 px per unit at 64x64 (79.5 at the 160x160 on the ASI662MM, 15.5 at the old 32x32). Only affects the px figures in the report, never the slope.
pipeline._volts_per_unit: the DAC scale of the driven channel, +1.0 for y below. Reporting only -- it converts the slope into px/V and mV/px and carries the optical sign.

params.config: y/tip DC gain through the PARPORT DAC (DAC81404, spi link, mmio, +-5 V range, mirror parked at 0 V), no coarse stage, ch0=y driven at scale 1.0 V/unit / ch1=x parked. ASI290MM 64x64 ROI 1084/418, exp 400, gain 0, fs ~2310 Hz, fit_com 55x55 sigma_init 6.55. Compare the slope against fsm_bodey_par2.dat's small-signal plateau 3.646 -- NOT against that file's 3.523 fit line, which is a large-signal number (y compresses ~4% above ~50 mV) -- and ONLY IF par2 was taken at this ROI SIZE, since K is normalized and rescales with (dim-1)/2. This slope, not par2, is what goes into steering_par_fsp.json's y.K.

pipeline._note: PARPORT DAC, wired exactly as steering_par_fsp.json: ch0 = y/tip, ch1 = x/tilt, scale [1, -1], offset 0. The scale signs MUST match the steering config -- the whole point of this run is to produce a K for that file, and a different sign convention here would produce a K with the wrong sign for it.
pipeline._range: +-5 fixed. Auto-ranging is deliberately NOT enabled: a mid-sweep range change glitches the output for a frame and steps the quantization, which would land in a settled level as a bogus point. The sweep never leaves +-0.12 V anyway. 153 uV/LSB over the +-5 V span = 0.019 px, four orders below the 1.5 px step.
pipeline._avss_note: AVSS must be -12 V on this rig for the bipolar range, as in every other parport_dac config here.
